how_customers_find_and_choose: Customers choose a nearby agent or shop on trust, queue length and how clearly staff explain what they are doing
Map listing and reviews matter for walk-in services; people check hours and wait time
Customers prefer to ask a question in chat first, then visit for anything needing documents or identity checks
Word of mouth and a reputation for honesty are the main drivers; mistakes spread fast
what_works_now: Clear, visible information on what the shop or agent can and cannot do, and the steps and documents needed
A quick chat reply with the opening hours, the documents to bring and the expected time
Receipts and written confirmation for every transaction
A saved list of regular customers told of due dates, renewals or reminders, with consent
A complete map listing with hours and accurate location
Polite handling of complaints with a clear person responsible
For field teams: a simple daily record of visits and collections
outdated_or_weak: Aggressive sales calls or repeated promotional messages
Vague or unclear explanations of charges or terms
Giving advice on regulated products beyond what the licence allows
Printed handbills as the main way to attract customers
Asking customers to share sensitive details in chat

PK: Cash on delivery and cash at the counter are still common; bank transfer and mobile wallet payments are now normal for many customers
Ramadan and the two Eids reshape demand, opening hours and staff availability every year
Summer heat, monsoon rain and power cuts affect operations and footfall
Customers often write in Urdu, Roman Urdu or a regional language, and chat is the usual first contact
Mobile wallets and bank transfers are widely used; customers often need help and trust the local agent
Financial and telecom services are regulated by their authorities; the owner confirms specifics with them
Eid and remittance seasons raise demand
UAE: Customers are multilingual and expect quick replies in chat; card and tap payments are normal
Winter is the busy season; many residents travel in summer so demand can dip
Ramadan and Eid change hours and buying patterns; the licence a business holds decides what it may sell and advertise, so the owner checks that with the licensing body
Remittance and exchange are busy; services are regulated by the central regulator and licensing authority
Customers are multilingual and expect clear receipts
CA: Customers expect online booking or enquiry, card and bank e-transfer payment, and clear written confirmation
Long winters and a short summer peak shape outdoor and seasonal trades
English and French (in Quebec) matter, and many communities prefer their own language; consent for marketing messages and sales tax rules vary, so the owner checks them with a professional
Financial and insurance services are tightly regulated by province; the owner confirms specifics
Internet and telecom customers compare plans and service quality online

never_assume: An approved process for any customer's sensitive data
